title: A followed shell's position is stored physically, so a later relative `cd ..` after a cd through a link is resolved where bash's logical cd does not go
outcome: engram_settle_shell_move anchors a followed shell at the canonical (physical) path that engram_resolve_shell_move returns. After a lone `cd /repos/a/link`, where link points to /repos/b/sub, TermAl presumes /repos/b/sub. A later lone `cd ..` is then resolved from there to /repos/b, while bash's default logical cd lands in /repos/a. Credit and overlap then follow the wrong worktree for that shell. engram_resolve_shell_move already refuses a `..` within one target whose logical and physical readings differ. The gap is across commands, because only the physical position is kept. Pre-existing in base 13c7023. Found out of scope by the Codex reviewer of PI-26a round 3 (delegation-3cc1c406, session-8365). That change no longer bounds any relative target of a lost line, so it does not widen this gap.
acceptance: The followed shell keeps the logical path it was moved to (as bash's `cd -L` would), or marks its position unknown when a link lies on it, so a later relative `cd ..` is resolved where bash lands or TermAl stops following; a regression test covers a lone cd through a link followed by a lone cd .. across two commands
